newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linde says considering fifth division.
newsitem.headline: Linde says considering fifth division.

text.p: German forklift truck maker Linde AG said on Thursday it planned to make large acquisitions, mostly abroad, to expand in its four existing divisions and to create a new, fifth division.

Chief executive Hans Meinhardt told a news conference Linde sees potential for sales growth by up to 70 percent to as much as 13 billion marks or 14 billion marks in the next five years, but that it would need to add a new division to achieve its goal of growing even further.

Linde would expand its four divisions which are currently, planned construction, cargo handling equipment, refrigeration, and technical gases, through a combination of organic growth as well as small and large takeovers, he said.
"Larger acquisitions will be made in our existing divisions...and we still regard a fifth division as necessary," he said.
Meinhardt did not specify what areas of activity the fifth division would be involved in, but said it would result from a foreign acquisition.
Meinhardt said in 1996 there were times when Linde thought it would be able to finalise a takeover soon, but the plans did not succeed.
"You have to patient. We don't plan unfriendly takeovers although there can always be a situation where you are forced into it. But it is not our company's style, especially not abroad," he said.
